claim: a status line on the author's own site saying an open-source tool now warns about a setting problem, a check the author proposed upstream and the maintainer shipped on 5 Nov
truth: The change was merged to the tool's main branch on 2026-11-05 but was in no release: the same run's package-registry read hours later showed the latest version was still the one published 2026-10-11, and the newest release builds were from that day too. The check first reached users in the next version, published 2026-11-08 01:37Z, whose package contains it (read 2026-11-10). The claim-time reads were the issue's close event and the merge, which show the code landed, not that anyone could install it
label: unsupported
caught_by: the same run's package-registry check, before the next run
would_catch: the package registry's latest version and date, or the release list

claim: a status line on the author's own site saying an open-source tool will warn about a setting problem: a check the author proposed upstream, merged by the maintainer on 5 Nov for the next release
truth: Merged 2026-11-05 04:28Z and unreleased at claim time; the next version, published 2026-11-08 01:37Z, contains the check (its package read 2026-11-10)

label: unsupported
